newsitem.title: USA: Cooper Cameron sees 1997 EPS about double 1996.
newsitem.headline: Cooper Cameron sees 1997 EPS about double 1996.

text.p: Cooper Cameron Corp said Thursday that given the strength in its markets, it expects its improved second quarter results to be sustainable over the next several quarters.
Sheldon Erikson, chairman, president and chief executive officer, said this will translate into continued improvement in the company's overall profitability.
"The current level of operations and backlog indicates that full year 1997 earnings per share should be approximately double the 1996 results, adjusted for the stock split," he said.
As of June 30, the company said its backlog was about $852 million, up from $633 million a year ago and $812 million at the end of the first quarter.
"Orders in the second quarter were only slightly below the previous period's record levels," Erikson said .

It was the fifth consecutive quarter of favorable year-over-year comparisons, he said, and confirms the company's expectations that the Cameron segment alone will exceed $1.0 billion in revenue this year.
The company also said it expects the improved margins at its Cameron and Cooper Energy Services segments to be sustainable.
Erikson said much of Cameron's improved profitability stems from volume leverage and improved pricing.

"Overall, Cameron's revenue increased more than 60 percent, and all regions and product lines demonstrated a minimum of 40 percent revenue growth, improved operating margins and growth in EBITDA compared with last year," he said.
The increase in activity in all of Cameron's markets has led to a tightening of capacity, extended lead times and higher prices, he added.

Erikson said the compression and power equipment segment's energy-related operations, performed by Cooper Energy, posted increased revenues and earnings because of higher activity levels in the large gas turbine and compressor project business.

The Turbocompressor division continues to generate excellent returns due to a stable market for both plant air and air separation units, he said. The division also benefited from the first phase of a previously announced manufacturing capacity expansion project, he said.
